title: Embedded clean-tape digit writer
statement: For any types $Q$ and $T$ with decidable equality, there are a natural number $K$, a finite state set $S$ with decidable equality, a machine $R$ with $K+1$ work tapes over symbols encoding digits, marked work cells, states, or tags, designated states $entry,exit\in S$, and a natural number $C$. For every $k$, embedding $\iota:\{0,\ldots,K\}\hookrightarrow\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, Boolean word $x$, and configuration $d$ on the encoded input, if $d$ begins in state $entry$ with input head at position $1$ and every cell of every tape in the image of $\iota$ blank, then the machine obtained by placing $R$ on those embedded tapes reaches a configuration equal to $d$ except that its state is $exit$ and tape $\iota(0)$ stores the binary expansion of $|x|+1$ from its initial head position. It does so by some time $t\le C(|x|+1)$, does not visit $exit$ earlier, and all work-tape heads remain within distance $C(\operatorname{bits}(|x|+1)+1)$ of their initial positions through time $t$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite state set $S$ with decidable equality exists
Embedding of $K+1$ tape indices into $k$ tape indices
Input is a Boolean word encoded as digit symbols
Every cell on each embedded tape is blank
Final configuration and contents of tape $\iota(0)$
